text:
Alex: FYI — we've got an escalated customer (acme-corp) hitting intermittent 401s when validating inbound bearer tokens. Started at ~2024-11-05T13:42:10Z. Error in our logs is 'no matching key found in JWKS (kid: K-rot1234)'. filing here to coordinate triage.
Maria: Can you paste the raw token header (just the header bits) and the middleware error lines? Also which jwks_uri they're configured with.
Alex: header (decoded): {
  "alg": "RS256",
  "kid": "K-rot1234"
}

Middleware log excerpt:
```
time=2024-11-05T13:42:11Z level=error svc=auth middleware=jwt msg="verification failed" err="no matching key found in JWKS (kid: K-rot1234)" correlation_id=acme-req-7b1c
```
Customer jwks_uri: https://auth.acme-corp.example/.well-known/jwks.json

Jordan: correlation_id noted. Is this happening for all tokens from acme-corp or only a subset? Any pattern by region/edge? Also, what is our current JWKS cache TTL for external providers?

Alex: It looks bursty — ~40 requests over a 2m window, then recovered. All regions. Current cache TTL = 5m (300s) with ETag support. We also saw some tokens with iat ~30s in the future compared to our verify node's clock. Stack traces point to our verify library returning 'kid not found' (we don't retry fetch on that path).

Samira: My initial guess: key rotation at acme -> they rotated keys and pushed new kid but our instance still had old JWKS in cache. Two contributing issues: 1) we don't proactively re-fetch on kid-miss, 2) small clock skew causes nbf/iat failures for tokens issued by some of their edge nodes. We should implement a fallback flow: on 'kid not found' -> immediately refetch jwks_uri (bypass cache) and retry verification once. Also add configurable leeway to JWT time checks (default 120s) and make JWKS TTL per-issuer configurable (min 60s for rotation-prone customers).

Chris: Agree. Also consider respecting Cache-Control/Expires + ETag/If-None-Match so we don't hammer jwks_uri for normal traffic. But for kid-miss the refetch should use If-None-Match (but bypass local stale cache if ETag mismatch). If they rotated keys, the endpoint will return new JWKS and we update.

Maria: We need to be careful about attackers trying to force our service to refetch JWKS repeatedly. Add rate-limiter per-issuer for forced refetch (e.g., 1 forced refetch per 30s per issuer) and log when forced refetch occurs (correlation id included). Also capture response status and whether the key appeared to avoid blind loops.

Jordan: Can you include exact repro steps so support can gather evidence and we can reproduce in staging? I'll want a curl sample and the sequence we used.

Alex: Repro steps I used locally:
1) Get a token signed with rotated key (kid: K-rot1234). Saved token as ROTATED_TOKEN.
2) Start auth service with jwks cache TTL=300s and pre-populate cache from current jwks_uri (no K-rot1234 present).
3) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROTATED_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.test/endpoint

Curl output snippet:
```
> GET /endpoint HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.test
> Authorization: Bearer <ROTATED_TOKEN>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: acme-req-7b1c
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "error_description": "no matching key found in JWKS (kid: K-rot1234)"
}
```
Server debug log during that request shows we did NOT attempt a network fetch because our cache still had an ETag and we honored it as fresh.

Samira: Example pseudo-code for the fallback (to put in a PR):
```
verify_jwt(token, issuer) {
  header = decode_header(token)
  jwks = jwks_cache.get(issuer)
  if !jwks.has_key(header.kid) {
    if forced_refetch_rate_limiter.allow(issuer) {
      remote_jwks = http.fetch(jwks_uri, headers={If-None-Match: jwks.etag})
      if remote_jwks.status == 200 {
        jwks_cache.update(issuer, remote_jwks.body, remote_jwks.etag)
      } else if remote_jwks.status == 304 {
        // no change
      }
    }
    // retry once against refreshed cache
    if !jwks_cache.get(issuer).has_key(header.kid) {
      raise VerificationError("no matching key found in JWKS (kid: %s)", header.kid)
    }
  }
  // proceed with normal verify with leeway
  return verify_with_leeway(token, leeway_seconds=config.leeway)
}
```

Chris: Good. Add tests for:
- kid-miss triggers remote fetch and succeeds when new key available
- kid-miss with remote 304 should not keep retrying
- rate-limiter prevents frequent forced fetches
- leeway prevents iat/nbf failures for <= 120s skew

Maria: For compliance: add an audit log entry when we update an issuer's JWKS cache detailing previous ETag, new ETag, timestamp, and correlation_id for manual review. Also, notify customers that rotate keys frequently that we recommend either overlapping keys during rotation (double-signed) or reducing TTL.

Samira: I'll open a draft PR implementing forced-refetch-on-kid-miss + per-issuer forced-refetch rate limiter + configurable leeway + tests. Plan: code + unit tests in eng-runtime, stomping env var ENABLE_JWKS_FALLBACK=false by default for canary. I'll run canary on a small fleet first.

Jordan: Who's owning the support side to coordinate with acme-corp? We'll need their jwks rotation schedule, sample failing token, and logs. Support: please collect tokens (redact if needed), correlation ids, and time windows.

Alex: Support is collecting those now. I attached correlation ids we saw: [acme-req-7b1c, acme-req-7b1d, acme-req-7b2a]. They also provided a sample rotated token in a secure artifact. :lock:

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for branch jwks-fallback by Samira (canary=5%) at 2024-11-05T14:03:00Z

Samira: Update — canary shows expected behavior: on first kid-miss we do a forced refetch; in test where remote returned updated JWKS, verification succeeded and response was 200. Logging includes forced-refetch:true and remote_status:200. Will expand canary to 25% after QA signoff.

Chris: After rollout, let's monitor metric auth.jwt.kid_miss_count, auth.jwks.forced_fetch_count, and 401_by_issuer. We'll set alert if forced_fetch_count > baseline * 3 to catch abuse.

Maria: One more thing: change the default leeway to 120s (was 30s) and add per-issuer override. Document in runbook: how to respond to kid-miss incidents and check JWKS endpoint health (latency, 5xx rates).

Alex: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket with the logs and confirm with support once the canary is at 25%.

deploy-bot: canary deploy successful for jwks-fallback at 2024-11-05T14:25:12Z (rollout: 5% -> 25% pending)

Samira: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-runtime/pull/412 (WIP) — will request review from @Chris and @Maria. :rocket:

Jordan: Nice work. After full rollout, we should add an integration test that simulates key rotation and ensures zero downtime for overlapping key windows.

Alex: Copy — I'll follow up with support and close the loop with the customer once we confirm stability. :thumbsup:
